stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(A\) is \(64^{\circ}\) and the measure of angle \(B\) is \(72^{\circ}\). Point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\), and \(\overline{CD}\) bisects angle \(ACB\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ADC\)?
solution: The bisector splits it in half: angle \(ACD = 22^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is angle \(ACD\), half of angle \(ACB\), not angle \(ADC\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 44 - 22\); it uses the whole angle \(ACB\) in place of angle \(A\) in triangle \(ADC\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is angle \(BDC = 180 - 72 - 22\), the angle on the other side of \(\overline{CD}\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'B': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'B'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-64)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','B','C')-72)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','D')-ang('D','C','B'))<0.1
acd=Rational(180-64-72,2)
ans=180-64-acd
assert ans==94 and abs(ang('A','D','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
